#1497. GdS: Why Cisse’s position remains a dilemma despite continuous flow of goals

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

“I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”

Who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

Seems to me like his profile is that of a second striker or even a striker. He’s actually very good in controlling the ball and shielding it from his opponent. Whereas, at least at the moment (maybe because of the injury) he doesn’t seem so fast. Not like a natural winger.

The Frosinone game is this one where he didn’t look labored in his running. He is still not moving free when in an all out sprint yet.

I didn’t realize the injury was as severe as I infer here. So what I thought was uncorrected poor mechanics is actually residual mental defaults to protect and compensate.

So some time around March as a guess we will see how he moves when free of all that baggage. If he combines the ability to run like Rafa with the skill set and work rate we already see then it will be quite a thing to watch him develop!

Dare I say it? It’s exciting times to be a Milan supporter. Forza!

Camarda should learn from Pio Esposito & Cisse process

He is definitely best as an inverted left attacking midfielder. From there he can attack space in a very different way than a striker does, and will score more goals as a consequence.

If cisse was French or Portuguese, he would be a guaranteed starter with the output he’s showing us. But bc he’s Italian that’s why there’s a dilemma

And he is not a better option than Ramos. They are bringing him along exactly how they should and it’s working. #1496. McKennie fit for Fiorentina as Juventus chase a third straight win before the break

Weston McKennie is over the muscle problem that kept him out at AZ and is set to start in Florence on Sunday. A win would send Spalletti's depleted side into the international break on a three-match winning run.

Juventus close the round in Florence with a familiar midfielder back. Spalletti will hand Weston McKennie an immediate return to the side, Sky Sport Italia reports. The return comes at a useful moment for a squad that is still stretched.

#FiorentinaJuve 🔜 https://t.co/ST1eWZieA8

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 6, 2026

Celik and Conceição face late fitness checks and may only make the bench. Before the AZ match, Çelik was one of three Juventus players with at least two goals in this Europa League campaign, alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani. The club’s squad list had not yet been published.

Yildiz, Thuram, Locatelli, Grabara, Nico González and Ekhator are all unavailable. The expected shape is a 4-4-2. Vicario is in goal behind Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumí and Cabal. McKennie, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and Alajbegovic form the midfield, with Kolo Muani and Woltemade up front.

Spalletti will skip the usual pre-match press conference. The decision was put down only to the run of closely spaced fixtures.

Fiorentina have problems of their own. Parisi, Atta and Pongračić are out, and Atta will not return until after the break. Ranieri may be fit enough for the bench. The hosts sit just above the relegation zone, but they carry a threat in Franco Mastantuono. He has had 38 shots, 11 of them on target, this Serie A season. Only Nico Paz, Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal have had more in Europe’s top five leagues.

History favours the visitors. Juventus have won 82 Serie A meetings with Fiorentina, the Viola have won 37, and 55 have been drawn. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against them, two fewer than Inter’s 277. A two-goal haul on Sunday would draw them level.

Kolo Muani looks the likeliest source. He has scored five of his last six Serie A goals away from home. Since February 2025, no Juventus player has more away league goals than his five, a tally that equals Dusan Vlahovic’s. He is also the only player at the club this season with at least three goals and three assists in all competitions, with four goals and three assists. He scored with Koopmeiners at AZ, taking Juventus to 11 goals after four Europa League matches.

Kerim Alajbegovic has a milestone within reach. He can become the first foreign player in Juventus’s history to score in two top-flight games in a row before turning 20.

The stakes are clear. Victory would carry Juventus into the break with three wins in a row and strengthen their bid to rejoin the European race. After it, Juventus host Venezia on 22 November at 12:30, before a trip to Como on 29 November.

#1495. Rodrigo Bentancur transfer: Aston Villa 'pursuit' of £8.4m-valued player could 'trigger' Tottenham Hotspur exit

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 02:12

Argentine giants Boca Juniors are reportedly keen to bring Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur back to Buenos Aires as they prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

While funding a deal for the 29-year-old Uruguay international would normally prove difficult, the potential sale of highly rated youngster Milton Delgado could hand Boca the financial firepower required.

Aston Villa are among a host of English clubs tracking the 21-year-old defensive midfielder, meaning a winter raid from Unai Emery's side could directly threaten Tottenham's midfield depth.

According to Argentine outlets El Crack Deportivo and El Intransigente via Sport Witness, Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme has already started preliminary work on re-signing Bentancur.

Riquelme views the Spurs stalwart as his preferred candidate to replace Delgado should the academy graduate depart La Bombonera in the coming months.

Bentancur progressed through Boca's youth ranks before earning a switch to Juventus in 2017 and is seen as the ideal experienced presence to anchor their upcoming continental campaign.

The South American outfit plan to reinvest the proceeds from Delgado's prospective transfer straight into a formal approach for their former player.

Delgado's stock has risen even further after he played the full 90 minutes in Boca's 2-0 Copa Sudamericana final triumph over Atletico Mineiro on Saturday.

Villa are reportedly preparing a formal January offer for Delgado after scouting the 21-year-old extensively across the past six months.

However, Emery's side are far from alone in the race, with Chelsea, Bournemouth, Brighton and West Ham United all linked with the youngster.

Boca are believed to have previously rejected a £7.5m bid from MLS side Atlanta United back in August, around the same time Chelsea and Bournemouth lodged initial enquiries for the young midfielder, who is valued at €10m (£8.4m) by Transfermarkt.

Portuguese outfit Porto are also believed to be monitoring developments from Europe, leaving Riquelme in a strong position to command a substantial fee if a bidding war erupts.

Even if Boca secure the necessary funds, convincing Bentancur to leave North London could prove complicated given that he signed a new long-term contract with Tottenham in October 2025 and has spent almost a decade competing at the top level in Europe.

#1494. Spalletti skips Fiorentina preview as Juventus seek a first win over Vanoli

Luciano Spalletti will not hold his eve-of-match press conference before Sunday's trip to Fiorentina. Juventus arrive on two straight wins, chasing fourth place, against a coach Spalletti has never beaten.

Juventus will travel to Florence without the usual preview from their coach. Sunday’s game at the Franchi kicks off at 20:45. The squad got back to Turin overnight from the Netherlands. The reason given is the club’s crowded run of fixtures, TuttoJuve reported. It is the last game before the international break.

The run began with a 2-0 win over Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on 1 November. Kerim Alajbegovic scored in the 70th minute. Aged 19 years and 41 days, no foreign player had ever found the net at a younger age in a Serie A game between Juventus and Napoli.

Four days later, Juventus won 2-1 away at AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League. Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani scored. The result takes them to 10 points from four games in the competition. After the match, Spalletti described himself as very pleased with a solid team display against strong opponents. He felt his side should have added a third goal.

The league position still needs work. The club’s stated aim this season is fourth place, and Como currently hold that spot. The defence gives some grounds for confidence. Going back to last March, no side can match the Bianconeri’s tally of 12 shutouts. Roma are next on 11.

Vanoli and Spalletti have faced each other only twice as coaches. Both meetings were Fiorentina-Juventus fixtures last season. Last November they drew 1-1 at the Franchi. Filip Kostic gave Juventus the lead before Rolando Mandragora equalised with a long-range shot.

The hosts’ struggles on their own pitch offer Juventus an opening against a side yet to find its footing at home.

The fixture carries plenty of history. Sunday’s game is the 175th Serie A meeting between the sides, according to the club’s statistical preview. Juventus have won 82, Fiorentina 37, and 55 have ended level. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against Fiorentina. Two more would draw them level with Inter’s 277, the highest total by any side against the Viola.

Once the international break is over, Juventus’s next Serie A match is on 22 November.

#1492. Erling Haaland sees Man City equaliser DISALLOWED in controversial circumstances - with fans and pundits split over whether Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno had both hands on the ball after fumbled strike

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026

Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney said her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she said: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

Erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z

Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham

'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'

Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

He said: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'

The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'

They added that the VAR said: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'

The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

Not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same

An Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'

A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

Not everyone agreed, though, with many X users taking the opposite stance.

One said: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'

Another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'

City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

#1491. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

Aug 30: Leeds United vs BrentfordSep 5: Brighton and Hove Albion vs Leeds UnitedSep 14: Leeds United vs Newcastle UnitedSep 19: Leeds United vs Crystal PalaceOct 10: Arsenal vs Leeds United

Aug 29: Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestSep 5: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham HotspurSep 12: Aston Villa vs Nottingham ForestSep 19: Nottingham Forest vs CoventryOct 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

The hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

#1488. Chelsea transfer news: PSG back off from Blues target

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 06:28

In recent seasons, Manu Kone has often been linked with Paris Saint-Germain, but the capital club have never really tried to sign him. The reason behind that choice has been revealed.

A talented French international from the Paris region, Manu Kone seemed to have the ideal profile to join PSG. The Roma midfielder has often been reported on the capital club's shortlist, but PSG have never really tried to recruit him.

The 25-year-old will return to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday at 8pm UK time, for matchday five of the Champions League with the Italian side.

He will have the chance to show the full extent of his talent to Parisian supporters, although it is unlikely that Kone will join the two-time European champions in the short term, according to L'Equipe.

The sports daily tried to explain the reasons for PSG's choice not to sign the French midfielder. This summer, Paris simply had no desire to recruit another midfielder and wanted to count on their current squad, with its established players such as Vitinha and Joao Neves, and its young gems such as Dro Fernandez and Senny Mayulu.

Paris had an opportunity in the summer of 2024. Before his move to Roma for £15.3m (€18m), the Frenchman was offered to Paris. Some people internally pushed for the capital club to sign this promising and affordable young box-to-box midfielder. Luis Campos has always liked the profile of the former Toulouse player.

However, PSG decided otherwise. 'I do not make all the decisions on my own' - the Paris sporting director said.

L'Equipe concludes that Luis Enrique did not approve the option. The Spanish boss preferred to rely on his Neves-Vitinha-Ruiz trio. Therefore, unless he changes his mind, the Kone option appears to be one to forget in Paris.

While PSG appear to have moved on, Kone has regularly been linked with clubs in England. Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United were all credited with interest in the Roma midfielder during the summer transfer window, including on deadline day, according to the Liverpool Echo.

Chelsea were said to still have an interest in late August, with Kone one of several midfielders on their list, according to CaughtOffside. At that stage, the website considered Manchester United effectively out of the race after the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, although that was its own assessment rather than a reported club position.

More recently, Gazzetta dello Sport reported in mid-November that Chelsea could make a move in January. Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini reportedly vetoed a sale in the final hours of the summer window, and the Italian club are said to value Kone at £47m-£51m (€55m-€60m), compared with the £43m reported in August.

#1487. Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

The hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

The table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s plans.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His new contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

The next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

#1486. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

“We have a CLEAR long-term plan and we won’t change it because of the table.”

From a fans point of view, if one big signing is the difference between scudetto and not scudetto, I would tend to disagree with Amorim.

I think his point is that it’s about making the right signings. ACM has made panic buys the last couple of years. Stick to the plan. I think Arsenal is the perfect example of this approach.

Yeah, Joao Felix and Santi GImenez were big money, so was Nkunku. But if they don’t have the right characteristics and don’t fit the squad, then they will be a net negative to the team as a whole,

#1485. Mauricio Pochettino's Man United rallying cry: New boss promises fans it will be a 'SPECIAL' season - despite club sitting in drop zone - as he gets straight to work after flying from US

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 21 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

The new Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

And during a busy first day among his new surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he said via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6

Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their new head coach

The new Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday

'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'

In a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'

Those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

Speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino said: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'

The club then officially welcomed the new manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'

Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour

The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am

The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino)

'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'

'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'

Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something important for the future of soccer in this country.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United

'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made new friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'

Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'

Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to quickly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note

The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino said after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'

Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a new contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1483. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

#1482. CM: Gimenez could terminate Porto loan early and return to Milan – the situation

Santiago Gimenez left AC Milan in the summer, but he may be returning before the end of his loan deal next summer.

It’s fair to say that Gimenez is one of the most difficult signings to assess from Milan in recent years. On paper, it made plenty of sense why he was right to arrive; he was firing in the Champions League, he had no difficulty scoring in the league and there was the added bonus of him being young and a fan of the club.

With goals against elite teams in Europe too, it made sense why he’d be able to have a successful career at San Siro. Performing on the biggest stage seemingly wasn’t an issue.

So, when he started brightly, fans thought the Rossoneri had struck gold. Yet, that form quickly came undone and Gimenez began to show glimpses, rather than actually developing a portfolio of goalscoring.

After almost being forced out of the club last summer, an injury-ridden campaign effectively ended his time with the Diavolo and he was loaned out in the summer. Yet, he could already be heading back to Italy.

As Calciomercato.com writes, it’s highly unlikely that Porto will activate the €18m buy clause in his deal, and it’s even possible that he doesn’t see out the complete spell of his loan. He’s the third-choice striker, with only four appearances in the Portuguese top flight and one penalty goal; it’s hardly form that warrants making his stay permanent.

Now, ahead of the January mercato, a meeting is planned with Rafaela Pimenta to discuss what would be best for his career. A return to Milanello cannot be ruled out, but it wouldn’t be permanent. He’s not part of Ruben Amorim’s plans, so a new destination would need to be found.

What is for sure, though, is that his value has only dropped further with his Portuguese adventure…

#1481. Inter: it’s unclear for Marcus Thuram

Between Marcus Thuram and Inter Milan, the love story started with the Frenchman’s arrival in the summer of 2023, and his association with Lautaro Martinez has borne fruit. The former Guingamp player has started his 4th season with the Nerazzurri, and it is time to discuss a contract extension, with the current one ending in 2028.

However, according to La Gazzetta dello Sportthe discussions turned out to be more complicated than expected. Thuram hopes for a salary increase, which Inter is reluctant to give other than through individual and collective bonuses. Especially since in 2028, Thuram will be 31 years old, and the Italian club already has his successor on the squad, in the person of Italian international Pio Esposito. So, will the love story really continue?

#1480. Lazio lose Tavares and Sutalo for at least three weeks as Juventus chase 11-point gap

Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

Not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026

Two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

Those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.
